body:
### Summary

When using `uv sync --frozen`, I want to be able to override the location from which packages are installed (defined  in URLs in my frozen uv.lock file) using the `UV_INDEX` environment variable or the `--index` command line argument. This is particularly useful in air-gapped networks or on networks where pypi.org/pythonhosted.org are unreachable. I think this behavior should also apply to `uv run --frozen <cmd>` when the auto-syncing of packages occurs. In my case, not being able to override the indexes is forcing me to manually manage my venv in my air-gapped network, which half defeats the purpose of using uv. 

I have a repository that is mirrored to an air-gapped network. My uv.lock file is built and committed to my project repo on an internet facing machine before being mirrored. The python dependencies for building/running the project are mirrored to a GitLab python registry that in no way matches the paths within my lock file (pypi.org/pythonhosted.org). Rebuilding my lock file on the air-gapped network is not feasible because not all dependencies for all groups and all python versions are mirrored on the air-gapped network, just the versions for the version of python I'm using.

Design details:
- In order for packages from overridden indexes to be synced, they need to match the name, version and hash from the uv.lock file
- Index overrides take precedence over the URL listed in the lock file. If they don't exist, fall back to the URL in the lock file
- The lock file will not be modified because the `--frozen` flag is in use in these cases


### Example

When a user is using a frozen uv.lock file in an air-gapped network or on a corporate network using a proxy PyPi registry, currently they must manually manage their virtual environment because `uv sync --frozen` will refuse to accept index overrides. With the requested changes, a user could set up some environment variables (UV_INDEX and optionally UV_INDEX_MYINDEX_USERNAME and UV_INDEX_MYINDEX_PASSWORD) and then `uv sync --frozen` and `uv run --frozen <cmd>` would behave and sync dependencies as if the user were on the internet. The user would no longer have to manually manage the virtual environment.

```
export UV_INDEX=myindex=https://mygitlab.org/api/v4/projects/4/packages/pypi
export UV_INDEX_MYINDEX_USERNAME=<gitlab-username>
export UV_INDEX_MYINDEX_PASSWORD=<gitlab-personal-access-token>

uv sync --frozen
```
In this example, uv would try to sync dependencies listed in the uv.lock file from `https://mygitlab.org/api/v4/projects/4/packages/pypi` first and then fall back to the URL listed in the uv.lock file.


### Example Code Changes
Here are some example code changes: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/compare/main...rxanp:uv:rxanp/allow-index-override-on-sync

title: Allow index override when using uv sync --frozen
